app_summary: A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs. Supported Operations: Create text post (optional media: image, video, shortened URL, user tag), Read post, Read entire user timeline, Receive recommendations on which users to follow, Search database for user or post, Register/Login using user credentials, Follow/Unfollow user

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: The user-service Kubernetes Service is misconfigured: the Service exposes port 9090 but its targetPort is set to 9999, while the user-service container listens on 9090. As a result the Service endpoints point to 10.244.1.30:9999 (no process listening) and calls from compose-post-service to user-service:9090 are forwarded to 10.244.1.30:9999 and get TCP connection refused (compose-post logs show repeated "TSocket::open() ... user-service Port: 9090: Connection refused").

args.root_cause: The user-service Kubernetes Service is misconfigured: the Service exposes port 9090 but its targetPort is set to 9999, while the user-service container listens on 9090. As a result the Service endpoints point to 10.244.1.30:9999 (no process listening) and calls from compose-post-service to user-service:9090 are forwarded to 10.244.1.30:9999 and get TCP connection refused (compose-post logs show repeated "TSocket::open() ... user-service Port: 9090: Connection refused").
args.evidence_summary: 1) Jaeger trace 0237bdefa5e96a3f shows a 500 error on /post/compose originating at nginx-thrift and involving compose-post-service in the call chain. 2) compose-post-service pod logs contain many errors: "TSocket::open() connect() <Host: user-service Port: 9090>: Connection refused" and repeated "Failed to connect user-service-client" entries. 3) kubectl describe service user-service shows Port: 9090 TargetPort: 9999 and Endpoints: 10.244.1.30:9999. 4) kubectl describe pod user-service-6d5985bd55-g79h4 shows the container listens on port 9090/TCP and is Ready. The mismatch (Service targetPort 9999 vs container 9090) explains the connection refused.
args.investigation_summary: I listed pods to confirm services running, checked traces for nginx-thrift to find an error, retrieved the detailed trace to identify the failing call path, fetched compose-post-service logs which showed connection refused errors to user-service:9090, listed services and described user-service to inspect ports and endpoints, and finally described the user-service pod to confirm its listening port. These steps show a Service targetPort/endpoint port mismatch causing caller connection failures.
